newsitem.title: SPAIN: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HARRISON BEATEN BY CUBAN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-OLYMPIC CHAMPION HARRISON BEATEN BY CUBAN.

text.p: Cuba's Yoelvis Quesada defeated Olympic triple jump champion Kenny Harrison with a dramatic last-round effort in an international athletics meeting on Wednesday.
Quesada, bronze medallist at last year's Atlanta Olympics, jumped 17.20 metres, a performance he alone has bettered during this indoor season.
The triple jump contest was the highlight of the Madrid Indoor Grand Prix meeting. Going into the last round, Quesada and compatriot Alliacer Urrutia had both achieved a best distance of 17.18.
Urrutia fouled while Quesada improved by two centimetres but both jumpers had to hold their breath as Harrison took the last jump of the contest.
Harrison came close but could not match Quesada's effort. He jumped 17.18 and claimed second place ahead of Urrutia on a count-back.
Russia's Irina Privalova ran the best women's 60 metres time of the year so far with a storming victory in 7.04 seconds.
Privalova flew out of the blocks and was never in danger. Ukraine's Zhanna Pintusevich was a distant second in 7.21 seconds.
Nigeria's Deji Aliu equalled the second-best men's 60 metres time of the year, clocking 6.55 seconds.
Aliu, the 1994 world junior 100 metres champion, just held off fast-finishing Briton Darren Braithwaite, who was second in 6.57.
Britain's Jason Livingston, in an international race for the first time since he completed a four-year ban for steroid abuse, finished fifth in 6.65 seconds.
American Andre Cason did not even make the main final in the stadium in which he set the current world best of 6.41 five years ago. He finished a disappointing third in his heat.
